item.title: Cape May with Everything on it — Mon Oct 19, 7:30 AM — NJ
item.description: Join Louise Zemaitis for this three-day birding workshop exploring Cape May during the best time of year for massive bird fallouts! This is the time at Cape May that the local birders wait for; visiting crowds of keen birders have diminished, yet the most massive bird fallouts of the season commonly occur NOW! Flocks of sparrows, kinglets, bluebirds, American Robins and Hermit Thrushes throng the trees and meadows – and it is now that knowledgeable birders start to sift through the birds in the hope of something really special, since this week starts the season for vagrants in Cape May. It’s also a great time for big raptors like buteos and Golden Eagles, while large seabird flights pass Avalon and Cape May Point nearly every day. Most of the three days will be spent outdoors, learning directly from our field experiences and much of our time will most likely be spent at some of Cape May’s key migration locations. item.title: Book Talk: Demystifying Disability with Emily Ladau — Mon Oct 19, 7:00 PM — Montclair Art Museum
item.description:
Join disability rights advocate, writer, and speaker Emily Ladau for a conversation about the newly revised and expanded edition of her book, Demystifying Disability, moderated by disability rights leader Rebecca Cokley, Director of the Ford Foundation’s U.S. Disability Rights program. With clarity, humor, and practical advice, Ladau tackles the questions many people have about disability but may be afraid to ask. From recognizing ableism and talking about disability to making accessibility part of everyday life, Demystifying Disability offers a thoughtful and accessible starting point for becoming a better ally. item.title: Book Talk: Becoming Roy Lichtenstein — Tue Oct 20, 7:00 PM — Montclair Art Museum
item.description:
Join art historian Avis Berman, author of the forthcoming Becoming Roy Lichtenstein: The Path to Pop, as she explores Roy Lichtenstein’s journey from an obscure artist to a defining figure of American Pop art. The Montclair Art Museum is excited to announce that Mythological Meeting, 1979, Lichtenstein’s only work held in the Museum’s collection, will be on view during Avis Berman’s book talk at MAM. Drawing on extensive archival research and hundreds of interviews, Berman traces Lichtenstein’s early influences, his search for an artistic identity, and the breakthrough that led to Look Mickey in 1961 and the development of his iconic style. The illustrated lecture will feature works of art alongside photographs of Lichtenstein, his friends, and family. Share this: Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook

item.title: Sparrow Sampler — Sat Oct 24, 7:30 AM — NJ
item.description: Join Michael O’Brien for this two-day workshop celebrating the ‘LBJs’ (little brown jobs) of the birding world. This is a workshop that celebrates the ‘LBJs’ (little brown jobs) of the birding world. Subtle and cryptic they might be; difficult to identify they are not, providing you have the right instructor, place and time. Early November at Cape May is a time when lots of sparrows of many species abound; common species like Swamp, Field, Savannah and Chipping, as well as uncommon ones like Clay-colored, Vesper, Lincoln’s, Nelson’s and Salt-marsh. Learn the first principals of size, shape and behavior, then practice examining plumage patterns to discover how stunning sparrows can be. Most of the two days will be spent outdoors, learning directly from our field experiences and much of our time will most likely be spent at some of Cape May’s key migration locations. item.title: Kill Goofy — Sun Oct 18, 1:30 PM — Grove Street Theater
item.description:
Apricot Sky Productions’s new play, Kill Goofy by Livingston playwright Eric Alter, opens October 9 and plays for three weekends throught October 25. The story is simple on the surface. Two best friends, inseparable at thirteen, haven’t spoken in thirty years. One of them never left his childhood bedroom. His mother never left because someone had to take care of him. Then the other one comes back to town, and everyone in that house has been keeping the same secret. It’s a play about the things we never say to the people closest to us, and it sends people out the door talking. Please note the play deals with difficult subject matter and is recommended for ages 15 and up. item.title: NEW DATE: Modern Calligraphy Workshop for Adults — Sun Oct 18, 2:00 PM — West Orange - Community Room 1
item.description:
Join The Spotted Canvas for a fun and relaxing Modern Calligraphy Workshop designed for beginners. Participants will learn the fundamentals of modern calligraphy, including proper pen technique, basic strokes, lettering, and how to connect letters to create beautiful words and phrases. Each participant will have the opportunity to practice their new skills and create their own personalized calligraphy piece to take home and enjoy.
No prior experience is necessary. All materials will be provided.

item.title: Cassandra: An Ongoing Tragedy, presented by Mosaic Dance Theater Company — Sun Oct 18, 3:00 PM — first congregation church
item.description:
Rich with emotional and social relevance, “Cassandra: An Ongoing Tragedy” by Ruth Cantrell contrasts Greek myths to modern day tragedies – war, terrorism, racism, sexual assault, gun violence, depicting the eternal existence of hate, and exploring the impact of the evils brought forth from Pandora’s Box. The stories in this piece are related by fictional characters in historical situations, through spoken word and dance, with an original score. Cast of 11. Oct 16 at 7pm, Oct 17 at 5pm, Oct 18 at 3pm. CONTENT WARNING This production shows graphic images of violence, including warfare, bombings, and their victims, with intense, jarring audio of gunfire and explosions. It is intended for mature audiences and those seeking to understand the events. Please take care of your well-being. Share this: Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook
